newsitem.title: USA: Kids list health care as concern - survey.
newsitem.headline: Kids list health care as concern - survey.

text.p: Providing medical care for anyone in need topped a list of issues that President Clinton should tackle, according to a survey of American children released Friday.

Cleaning up the environment, ending homelessness and preventing violence and terrorism ranked next in importance, said the survey of 501 children aged 9 to 12. It was conducted for Time for Kids magazine.
Asked what problem the president should solve by 2000, 12 percent said drugs, 10 percent said crime and 27 percent said they didn't know.
Most of the children gave Clinton an "A" for his performance but gave Congress a "B", it said.
Asked how they would spend an entire day with Clinton, 46 percent chose a visit to the White House to see what he does.

Nineteen percent wanted the president see how they spend their day, 14 percent wanted a ride on Air Force One, 13 percent wanted to watch a baseball or basketball game together and 8 percent wanted to met Chelsea Clinton, it said.

The children surveyed were optimistic about the future, with 73 percent saying they do not expect to fight in a war between the United States and another country. Sixteen percent said they thought they would.
The survey was conducted by New York-based Roper Starch Worldwide and appears in an issue of the the magazine, designed for classroom use, next week.
The survey entailed telephone interviews with 501 children between Dec. 5 and Dec. 15, 1996. The margin of error was plus or minus 4 percentage points.
